```text
Practice the way an exam feels: a fixed time, a pass mark and no going back.
A look at Exam simulation in LabGuide’s Student Pro.

In this video:
• Setting up an exam simulation: a required time limit and pass mark, questions drawn in proportion from all topics.
• Taking it: one question after another, with no question map, no marking and no going back.
• The report: pass or fail, total time, average time per question, the five longest questions, topics and the change against the previous simulation.

What LabGuide does today:
• Exam simulation is a Pro feature of the Student Pro plan (and Premium). The existing free Exam mode and the category test stay free and unchanged.
• A practice result is feedback for you, not an official grade or a real exam result.

Pro features: part of LabGuide’s optional paid plans (Student Pro, Teacher Pro, Specialist Pro, Premium), with a 7-day free trial where offered. Features that are free today stay free. Prices are shown in the App Store / Google Play.

Good to know:
• Questions come from the app’s question banks; the simulation does not copy any real exam.

LabGuide is a clinical-laboratory companion app for lab professionals and students (English, Russian, Uzbek). It is a learning and reference tool: it does not diagnose or interpret patient results.
```

## 10. End screen / CTA suggestion

* YouTube end screen (last ~7–20 s): subscribe + the next video in the SAME language edition (`premium_overview`, `teacher_pro`) + the playlist `[[LINK_PLAYLIST]]`. Place elements so they do not cover the end card's path pill or disclosure notices (check against the final scene).
* Description and pinned comment carry the store links (`[[LINK_APP_STORE]]`, `[[LINK_PLAY]]`); the video itself shows only the in-app path, no URL and no price.
* Instagram: link in bio (`[[LINK_BIO]]`); ask viewers to save/share, not to "download now".

## 11. Safe-content notes

* No patient data, names or real results anywhere. All numbers on screen are illustrative and labelled so.
* No third-party logo, brand name, stock footage or music. The only logo is the owner's app icon.
* Do not call the voice "natural", "professional" or "human": it is synthetic and nobody has listened to it yet.
* Do not call the content "approved", "verified", "certified" or "clinically validated": expert review is pending.
* No diagnosis, treatment, dosing or "normal range" statement. Reference ranges come from the user's laboratory.
* Do not answer individual medical questions in comments; point to the user's laboratory SOP, the reagent IFU and the clinician.
* No price, discount, product id or availability date in any text (docs/DECISIONS.md D-77/D-78: prices live in the stores).
* Check the platform's own disclosure setting for AI-generated / synthetic voice before posting (NEEDS_OWNER_CHECK: the rules change; the kit already states the voice is synthetic in the text).
* Audience: not made for kids. Category: Education. Comments: moderate; hide spam and requests for medical advice.
